purpose: Follow-up on probability quality along fixed-prediction correction powers; specified before fitting these paths. Earlier allocation outcomes already exist and are not represented as new prospectively recruited data.
selection: The first 60 of the existing 500 fixed five-row block permutations, selected for computational scope without searching these power-path outcomes.
block_convention: 240 source five-row blocks; not verified respondent IDs
prediction_policy: Existing cross-fitted nuisance routine fitted once per allocation and routine, frozen across powers; all fallback statuses retained. No new AI predictions or responses.
evaluation: The 3405 released rows beyond the 1200-row inference prefix. Their labels do not enter any fit in this follow-up. No verified person-disjoint sampling or population uncertainty is claimed.
reference: Human ridge with mean labelled logit loss plus ||beta||^2/(2*m), including every coefficient; same 20 human labels.
solver: Interior support check followed by stable exact gradient/Hessian Newton refinement, target Euclidean gradient residual <=1e-7*power. Retain failures and numerical boundary states.
separation: Replay the retained ordinary separation directions for these allocations and normalize to unit Euclidean norm. Use negative-margin mass explicitly in the robust finite-design lower bound.
scope: Conditional descriptive public-design diagnostic. Does not validate the Gaussian probability law, compare new estimators, or establish population predictive superiority. All allocations and powers retained.
